chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who bequeaths a will to another man, and the latter refuses to accept it, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not be abandoned in this state.'
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
A man whose father invited him to accept his will, is he allowed to refuse accepting his father's will? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'He is not allowed to refuse.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person to refuse accepting a bequest left to them by a relative?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between the obligation to accept a bequest and the preservation of kinship ties (silat al-rahim); specifically, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that a son cannot refuse his father's will, emphasizing the father's authority in testamentary disposition. The first narration highlights that refusal does not constitute a breach of family bonds, while the second establishes the binding nature of the father's directive, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the enforceability of the one-third bequest (wasiyyah) within the family structure.
